newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends near new contract lows.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends near new contract lows.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures ended lower but above their new contract lows, boosted by a light short-covering rally toward the close, traders said.

Wheat values eroded throughout the session on a combination of bearish factors: news that Egypt bought 450,000 tonnes of French wheat, spillover pressure from CBOT soybeans and an increase in hedge-type selling.
"We saw a lot of elevator-type stuff today. I guess the farmers picked up their cash sales," a trader said.
Egypt's purchase of French wheat was done at values that were $10 to $15 cheaper than U.S. prices, exporters said.
MGE spring wheat closed five to 12 cents per bushel lower, with Sept down 12 cents at $4.24. Dec set a new contract low at $4.04-1/2, before closing at $4.07, down 6-1/2 cents.

Traders said Wilson Trading bought two million Dec bushels and sold 1.5 million Dec. Benson-Quinn bought and sold 1.5 million Dec. Traders reported seeing a fair amount of buying MGE spring wheat on the intermarket spread with Chicago.
MGE estimated Monday's spring wheat volume at 21.48 million bushels, versus 24.53 million on Friday.
MGE barley closed unchanged to 11 cents per hundredweight lower, with Dec down eight cents at $7.23.
